From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Discovery recap - Observability & Evals (Ava Health)

Thanks again for taking the time earlier, Kate — really appreciate the context. Quick recap of what we discussed and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Pain points you mentioned:
- Hard to detect generation regressions after model updates (false positives/negatives from current QA).
- Lack of end-to-end observability tying prompts -> model outputs -> downstream app errors.
- Occasional 95/99p latency spikes that affect UX during peak hours.
- Need for cost transparency per request to justify model choices to the exec team.

Current stack you shared:
- AWS EKS (customers routed via ALB)
- Redis for session state + short-term KV cache
- Datadog for infra metrics; Sentry for app errors
- Internal QA pipeline runs unit tests but no golden-prompt regression harness yet

Success criteria (what would make this a win):
- Regression alerts that catch behavioral regressions with <1 week false positive rate at <5%
- Dashboards showing per-route token costs and p99 latency under 400ms for interactive flows
- Ability to run controlled evals on a golden set and measure quality deltas after model changes
- Clear rollout guardrails (canary %s, automatic rollback on objective regressions)

Observability & evals ask (from the call):
- Per-route dashboards (latency, tokens, cost, error rates) and a dedicated "golden prompts" dashboard to track eval metrics over time.
- Tracing hooks and headers we can add to instrument calls (X-Redwood-Trace or similar).
- Golden prompt set authoring + a CI-driven eval pipeline that triggers regression alerts.
- Regression alerting thresholds + policy for auto rollback during rollouts.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I’ll share a short evaluation plan and a sample golden prompt set for your team to review (attached).
2) Nikhil (cc’d) will propose the tracing/header wiring and dashboard metrics we recommend for Datadog integration.
3) Schedule a 30-45m technical sync with your infra/SRE (can do next week) to review integration constraints and staging traffic.
4) We’ll provide a rough cost/throughput estimate for running a 2-week eval in your staging environment.

Attachments: redwood-observability-eval-plan.pdf (eval approach, metrics, and timeline).

If I missed anything or if you want that technical sync included with specific folks from your side, let me know and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Kate Reynolds <kate@avahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap - Observability & Evals (Ava Health)

Hi Kate + Marissa — jumping in with a proposed technical plan and the minimal instrumentation to get the dashboards and evals running quickly.

Instrumentation basics:
- Add a tracing header: X-Redwood-Trace-ID (UUID) on every request from your frontend -> API -> model call.
- Pass request metadata as headers: X-Route-Name, X-User-Id (hashed), X-Session-Id. These feed into our KV cache keys and dashboard rollups.
- Sample payload entry in traces: {timestamp, route, prompt_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, status_code, redwood_trace_id} (we can provide a small JSON schema).

Datadog integration / dashboards:
- Recommended dashboards: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), token consumption per route, cost per route, error rate, model-version drift chart (quality delta vs golden set).
- Suggested alert rules: p99 latency > 400ms for >5m (notify on-call); golden-prompt regression: absolute drop in pass-rate > 3% vs baseline for 2 consecutive runs -> trigger pager and start rollback playbook.

Golden prompts + evals:
- Attached: sample-golden-prompts.json (small representative set we recommend you start with). We recommend keeping the set to ~200-500 prompts for early evals.
- Eval harness: run nightly/CI-driven evals comparing baseline model -> candidate model and compute per-prompt quality signals (pass/fail, semantic similarity, BLEU/ROUGE where relevant).
- Regression alerts should be tied to both statistical thresholds and manual review gates for high-impact flows.

Rollout guardrails:
- Canary rollout plan: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with automated checks at each step (latency, error rate, golden-set pass-rate).
- If any automated check fails (e.g., golden-set pass-rate drops > 3% or p99 spikes > 50% relative), auto-roll back and open an incident.

What I need from you to get started:
1) Sample staging traffic (anonymized) or a traffic profile (rps, typical prompt length) — we can work off rough numbers if you don’t have sample data handy.
2) Access or a contact to set up Datadog ingest for the traces (API key/scoped token or SRE contact).
3) Confirmation on the golden-prompt set owner (who will review/approve).

I’ll follow up with a short doc containing the JSON schema for the trace payload and a Datadog dashboard template you can import. Happy to run through this on a quick call with your SREs.

Cheers,
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
